ELDER ABUSE RESTRAINING ORDER — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Jordan Lee

PETITIONER, PROTECTED PERSON, RESPONDENT, AND INCIDENT DESCRIPTION
I, Jordan Lee, declare under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the following is true and correct. Jordan Lee is the elder or dependent adult these protective orders are sought to protect. If Jordan Lee is not Jordan Lee, Jordan Lee's relationship to Jordan Lee is: Adult child / conservator / attorney-in-fact / etc. The respondent is Pat Morgan. On or about August 15, 2026, at or near 123 Main St., Sacramento, CA, the following occurred: On March 3, 2026, the respondent appeared outside the petitioner’s home and yelled threats for several minutes before leaving. Additional incidents, if any: On March 10, 2026, the respondent sent several threatening text messages to the petitioner. This declaration describes conduct alleged in connection with a request for protective orders under California Welfare and Institutions Code section 15657.03, part of the Elder Abuse and Dependent Adult Civil Protection Act.

STATUTORY DEFINITIONS OF "ELDER" AND "DEPENDENT ADULT"
A petition for protective orders under the Elder Abuse and Dependent Adult Civil Protection Act, Welfare and Institutions Code section 15657.03, is available only on behalf of a person who meets one of two statutory categories. Section 15610.27 defines "elder" as any person residing in California who is 65 years of age or older — an age-and-residency test with no separate requirement of incapacity or vulnerability. Section 15610.23 defines "dependent adult" in two independent ways: first, as a California resident between 18 and 64 years old who has physical or mental limitations restricting the ability to carry out normal activities or protect one's rights, expressly including people with physical or developmental disabilities and people whose abilities have diminished because of age; second, regardless of any disability finding, as any person between 18 and 64 admitted as an inpatient to a 24-hour health facility as defined in specified Health and Safety Code sections. These are the same statutory definitions of "elder" and "dependent adult" used throughout the Act, including for a financial-abuse civil claim; here they set the threshold question of who the restraining-order remedy in section 15657.03 is available to protect.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "“Elder” means any person residing in this state, 65 years of age or older."
  — Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code § 15610.27 (California Legislative Information text), Welf. & Inst. C. § 15610.27 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=WIC&sectionNum=15610.27.)
  "(a) “Dependent adult” means a person, regardless of whether the person lives independently, between the ages of 18 and 64 years who resides in this state and who has physical or mental limitations that restrict his or her ability to carry out normal activities or to protect his or her rights, including, but not limited to, persons who have physical or developmental disabilities, or whose physical or mental abilities have diminished because of age."
  — Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code § 15610.23(a) (California Legislative Information text), Welf. & Inst. C. § 15610.23(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=WIC&sectionNum=15610.23.)
  "(b) “Dependent adult” includes any person between the ages of 18 and 64 years who is admitted as an inpatient to a 24-hour health facility, as defined in Sections 1250, 1250.2, and 1250.3 of the Health and Safety Code."
  — Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code § 15610.23(b) (California Legislative Information text), Welf. & Inst. C. § 15610.23(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=WIC&sectionNum=15610.23.)

This clause cites two code sections (§ 15610.27, a single subsection, and § 15610.23(a)-(b), two subsections of the same section); the two subsections of § 15610.23 are treated as one source, not independent corroborating sources, and § 15610.27 is treated as a second, independent source from a different code section. This clause states only the statutory definitions; it does not itself determine that any specific person is an "elder" or "dependent adult," or that any specific person is entitled to protective orders under section 15657.03.

STATUTORY DEFINITION OF "ABUSE OF AN ELDER OR A DEPENDENT ADULT"
Welfare and Institutions Code section 15610.07(a) defines "abuse of an elder or a dependent adult," for purposes of the entire Elder Abuse and Dependent Adult Civil Protection Act — including the restraining-order remedy in section 15657.03 — as any of three categories: (1) physical abuse, neglect, abandonment, isolation, abduction, or other treatment with resulting physical harm or pain or mental suffering; (2) the deprivation by a care custodian of goods or services that are necessary to avoid physical harm or mental suffering; or (3) financial abuse, as separately defined in section 15610.30. These three categories are independent alternatives, and the second is narrower than the first in one respect: it applies specifically to a "care custodian's" deprivation of necessary goods or services, not to a deprivation by any person. Section 15657.03(a)(1) conditions eligibility to petition for protective orders on the elder or dependent adult having "suffered abuse, as defined in Section 15610.07" — so this definition, rather than a separate restraining-order-specific abuse definition, is the operative standard for what conduct may support a petition under section 15657.03.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "(a) “Abuse of an elder or a dependent adult” means any of the following: (1) Physical abuse, neglect, abandonment, isolation, abduction, or other treatment with resulting physical harm or pain or mental suffering. (2) The deprivation by a care custodian of goods or services that are necessary to avoid physical harm or mental suffering. (3) Financial abuse, as defined in Section 15610.30."
  — Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code § 15610.07(a) (California Legislative Information text), Welf. & Inst. C. § 15610.07(a)(1)-(3) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=WIC&sectionNum=15610.07.)

This is a single statutory subsection (§ 15610.07(a)); no additional independent source was found for this. Subsection (b), stating only an operative date (July 1, 2016) for the current version of this definition, is not quoted or described here because it carries no substantive content. This clause states only the statutory definition; it does not itself determine that any specific conduct constitutes abuse of an elder or dependent adult, or that any specific person committed or suffered such abuse.

ELIGIBILITY TO PETITION: THE ELDER OR DEPENDENT ADULT, OR SPECIFIED OTHERS ON THEIR BEHALF
Welfare and Institutions Code section 15657.03(a) identifies who may bring a petition for protective orders under the Elder Abuse and Dependent Adult Civil Protection Act. Under section 15657.03(a)(1), the elder or dependent adult who has suffered abuse, as defined in section 15610.07, may petition on their own behalf. Under section 15657.03(a)(2)(A), a petition may also be brought on that person's behalf by one of four specified categories: a conservator or trustee of the elder or dependent adult, an attorney-in-fact acting within the authority of a power of attorney, a person appointed as a guardian ad litem, or "other person legally authorized to seek the relief." Section 15657.03(a)(2)(B) narrows that last, catch-all category for one specific type of petition: where the petition alleges abuse in the form of isolation, "other person legally authorized to seek the relief" also includes an "interested party" — defined in section 15657.03(b)(3) as an individual with a personal, preexisting relationship with the elder or dependent adult — but only for the purpose of seeking the isolation-specific order described in section 15657.03(b)(5)(E). Separately, section 15657.03(a)(3)(A) allows a petition to be brought on an elder or dependent adult's behalf by a county adult protective services agency, but only where the elder or dependent adult has suffered abuse and has an impaired ability to appreciate and understand the circumstances placing them at risk, or where the elder or dependent adult has given written authorization for the agency to act on their behalf. Two further defined terms from section 15657.03(b) describe the parties once a petition is filed: "Petitioner" means the elder or dependent adult to be protected — not necessarily the person who signed and filed the petition — and, if the petition is granted, the protected person; "Respondent" means the person against whom the protective orders are sought.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "(a) (1) An elder or dependent adult who has suffered abuse, as defined in Section 15610.07, may seek protective orders as provided in this section."
  — Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code § 15657.03(a)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Welf. & Inst. C. § 15657.03(a)(1) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=WIC&sectionNum=15657.03.)
  "(2) (A) A petition may be brought on behalf of an abused elder or dependent adult by a conservator or a trustee of the elder or dependent adult, an attorney-in-fact of an elder or dependent adult who acts within the authority of a power of attorney, a person appointed as a guardian ad litem for the elder or dependent adult, or other person legally authorized to seek the relief."
  — Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code § 15657.03(a)(2)(A) (California Legislative Information text), Welf. & Inst. C. § 15657.03(a)(2)(A) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=WIC&sectionNum=15657.03.)
  "(B) (i) Subject to clause (ii), if the petition alleges abuse of an elder or dependent adult in the form of isolation, the term “other person legally authorized to seek the relief” as used in subparagraph (A) includes an interested party as defined in paragraph (3) of subdivision (b). (ii) Clause (i) shall apply only for the purpose of seeking an order enjoining isolation under subparagraph (E) of paragraph (5) of subdivision (b)."
  — Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code § 15657.03(a)(2)(B) (California Legislative Information text), Welf. & Inst. C. § 15657.03(a)(2)(B) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=WIC&sectionNum=15657.03.)
  "(3) (A) A petition under this section may be brought on behalf of an elder or dependent adult by a county adult protective services agency in either of the following circumstances: (i) If the elder or dependent adult has suffered abuse as defined in subdivision (b) and has an impaired ability to appreciate and understand the circumstances that place the elder or dependent at risk of harm. (ii) If the elder or dependent adult has provided written authorization to a county adult protective services agency to act on that person’s behalf."
  — Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code § 15657.03(a)(3)(A) (California Legislative Information text), Welf. & Inst. C. § 15657.03(a)(3)(A) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=WIC&sectionNum=15657.03.)
  "(2) “Conservator” means the legally appointed conservator of the person or estate of the petitioner, or both. (3) “Interested party” means an individual with a personal, preexisting relationship with the elder or dependent adult. A preexisting relationship may be shown by a description of past involvement with the elder or dependent adult, time spent together, and any other proof that the individual spent time with the elder or dependent adult. (4) “Petitioner” means the elder or dependent adult to be protected by the protective orders and, if the court grants the petition, the protected person."
  — Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code § 15657.03(b)(2)-(4) (California Legislative Information text), Welf. & Inst. C. § 15657.03(b)(2)-(4) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=WIC&sectionNum=15657.03.)

Proc. § 527.6) or domestic violence (Fam. Code § 6211) statutes; the actual text authorizes only the elder or dependent adult, a conservator, a trustee, an attorney-in-fact under a power of attorney, a guardian ad litem, or an "other person legally authorized to seek the relief" (a catch-all, not an enumerated list of relatives), plus — narrowly, and only for an isolation-based petition — an "interested party" defined by a personal, preexisting relationship rather than family status, plus a county adult protective services agency under the two specific circumstances stated in section 15657.03(a)(3)(A). This clause also flags a defined-term subtlety: the statute's own definition of "Petitioner" in section 15657.03(b)(4) is the protected elder or dependent adult, not necessarily the person who signs and files the petition when someone else petitions on that person's behalf — a distinction this document's drafting clauses account for by separating the filer (the petitionerName field) from the protected person (the elderOrDependentAdultName field) as separate fields. This clause cites five subsections of the same statutory section (§ 15657.03(a)(1), (a)(2)(A), (a)(2)(B), (a)(3)(A), and (b)(2)-(4)); they are treated as one source, not independent corroborating sources. Subsections (a)(3)(B)-(C), addressing a required referral to the public guardian and confidentiality restrictions specific to a county adult protective services agency's petition, are not quoted or described in this clause. This clause states only the statutory eligibility categories; it does not itself determine that any specific person is eligible to petition, or that a specific filer falls within any of these categories.

RELIEF A PROTECTIVE ORDER MAY INCLUDE — PERSONAL CONDUCT ORDERS, RESIDENCE EXCLUSION, AND ITS LIMITS
Welfare and Institutions Code section 15657.03(b)(5) defines "protective order," for purposes of section 15657.03, to include several categories of restraining order, issuable ex parte, after notice and hearing, or in a judgment. Section 15657.03(b)(5)(A) authorizes a personal-conduct order enjoining a party from abusing, intimidating, molesting, attacking, striking, stalking, threatening, sexually assaulting, battering, harassing, telephoning (including annoying calls under Penal Code section 653m), destroying personal property, contacting (directly or indirectly), or coming within a specified distance of, or disturbing the peace of, the petitioner, and, on a showing of good cause, of other named family or household members or a conservator of the petitioner; the same subparagraph separately authorizes the court, on a showing of good cause, to grant the petitioner exclusive care, possession, or control of an animal, or to order the respondent to stay away from it. Section 15657.03(b)(5)(B) authorizes an order excluding a party from the petitioner's residence or dwelling — but this residence-exclusion order carries an express statutory limit: it may not be issued if legal or equitable title to, or a lease of, the residence is in the sole name of the party to be excluded, or in that party's name together with any other party besides the petitioner. Section 15657.03(b)(5)(C) authorizes an order enjoining other specified behavior the court determines necessary to effectuate either of the first two categories.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "(A) An order enjoining a party from abusing, intimidating, molesting, attacking, striking, stalking, threatening, sexually assaulting, battering, harassing, telephoning, including, but not limited to, making annoying telephone calls as described in Section 653m of the Penal Code, destroying personal property, contacting, either directly or indirectly, by mail or otherwise, or coming within a specified distance of, or disturbing the peace of, the petitioner, and, in the discretion of the court, on a showing of good cause, of other named family or household members or a conservator, if any, of the petitioner."
  — Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code § 15657.03(b)(5)(A) (California Legislative Information text), Welf. & Inst. C. § 15657.03(b)(5)(A) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=WIC&sectionNum=15657.03.)
  "(B) An order excluding a party from the petitioner’s residence or dwelling, except that this order shall not be issued if legal or equitable title to, or lease of, the residence or dwelling is in the sole name of the party to be excluded, or is in the name of the party to be excluded and any other party besides the petitioner."
  — Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code § 15657.03(b)(5)(B) (California Legislative Information text), Welf. & Inst. C. § 15657.03(b)(5)(B) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=WIC&sectionNum=15657.03.)
  "(C) An order enjoining a party from specified behavior that the court determines is necessary to effectuate orders described in subparagraph (A) or (B)."
  — Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code § 15657.03(b)(5)(C) (California Legislative Information text), Welf. & Inst. C. § 15657.03(b)(5)(C) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=WIC&sectionNum=15657.03.)

This clause cites three subparagraphs of a single statutory paragraph (§ 15657.03(b)(5)(A)-(C)); they are treated as one source, not independent corroborating sources. Section 15657.03(b)(5) also authorizes two further, narrower categories of order not described in this clause: subparagraph (D), available after notice and a hearing only, permits a finding that specific debts were incurred as a result of financial abuse; and subparagraph (E), also available after notice and a hearing only, permits an order enjoining a respondent from isolating the elder or dependent adult, but only on a three-part evidentiary showing and only in favor of an "interested party" as described in this document's eligibility clause, and never where the elder or dependent adult resides in a long-term care facility or is a patient of specified health facilities. This clause states only the categories of relief the statute authorizes; it does not itself determine which category of relief is appropriate for any specific petition, or that any specific order will issue.

STANDARD FOR AN ORDER, DURATION AND RENEWAL, AND THE CONSEQUENCE OF VIOLATING ONE
Welfare and Institutions Code section 15657.03(c) states the standard for a protective order under this section: with or without notice, an order may issue to restrain any person for the purpose of preventing a recurrence of abuse if a declaration shows, to the satisfaction of the court, reasonable proof of a past act or acts of abuse of the petitioning elder or dependent adult. This standard does not include a separate showing that "great or irreparable harm would result" absent an order — a phrase that appears in California's civil harassment TRO statute, Code of Civil Procedure section 527.6(d), but that is not part of section 15657.03(c)'s text. Once an order issues after notice and a hearing, section 15657.03(i)(1) allows a duration of not more than five years, and allows renewal, on a party's request, for either five additional years or permanently, without a showing of any further abuse since the original order issued; a renewal request may be made at any time within the three months before the order's expiration. Section 15657.03(i)(2) provides that an order silent on its expiration date defaults to a three-year duration from issuance. Separately, section 15657.03(x) states that willful disobedience of a temporary restraining order or restraining order after hearing granted under this section is punishable under Penal Code section 273.6.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]

  — Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code § 15657.03(c) (California Legislative Information text), Welf. & Inst. C. § 15657.03(c) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=WIC&sectionNum=15657.03.)

HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A CIVIL HARASSMENT OR DOMESTIC VIOLENCE RESTRAINING ORDER
Welfare and Institutions Code section 15657.03(y) states that section 15657.03 does not apply to any action or proceeding governed by Chapter 3 (commencing with Section 525) of Title 7 of Part 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure — the chapter that includes California's civil harassment restraining order statute, Code of Civil Procedure section 527.6 — or by Division 10 (commencing with Section 6200) of the Family Code, California's Domestic Violence Prevention Act. Section 15657.03's own eligibility structure, in turn, does not rest on the kind of relationship-based test that governs those two other statutes: it turns instead on whether the person to be protected is an "elder" (65 or older) or a "dependent adult," as defined in sections 15610.27 and 15610.23, and on whether that person has suffered "abuse," as defined in section 15610.07 — with no requirement, as there is for a domestic violence restraining order, that the parties be spouses, cohabitants, dating partners, co-parents, or relatives within a specified degree, and no requirement, as there is for a civil harassment restraining order, that the parties fall outside such a relationship. An elder or dependent adult abused by a spouse, an adult child, a caregiver, or a stranger can each potentially fall within section 15657.03's coverage, provided the abuse and elder/dependent-adult definitions are met; which statute in fact governs a given set of facts depends on the parties' actual relationship and the nature of the alleged conduct.

This section does not preclude a petitioner’s right to use other existing civil remedies."

expectedJSON.body: Welfare and Institutions Code section 15610.07(a) defines "abuse of an elder or a dependent adult," for purposes of the entire Elder Abuse and Dependent Adult Civil Protection Act — including the restraining-order remedy in section 15657.03 — as any of three categories: (1) physical abuse, neglect, abandonment, isolation, abduction, or other treatment with resulting physical harm or pain or mental suffering; (2) the deprivation by a care custodian of goods or services that are necessary to avoid physical harm or mental suffering; or (3) financial abuse, as separately defined in section 15610.30. These three categories are independent alternatives, and the second is narrower than the first in one respect: it applies specifically to a "care custodian's" deprivation of necessary goods or services, not to a deprivation by any person. Section 15657.03(a)(1) conditions eligibility to petition for protective orders on the elder or dependent adult having "suffered abuse, as defined in Section 15610.07" — so this definition, rather than a separate restraining-order-specific abuse definition, is the operative standard for what conduct may support a petition under section 15657.03.

expectedJSON.body: Welfare and Institutions Code section 15657.03(a) identifies who may bring a petition for protective orders under the Elder Abuse and Dependent Adult Civil Protection Act. Under section 15657.03(a)(1), the elder or dependent adult who has suffered abuse, as defined in section 15610.07, may petition on their own behalf. Under section 15657.03(a)(2)(A), a petition may also be brought on that person's behalf by one of four specified categories: a conservator or trustee of the elder or dependent adult, an attorney-in-fact acting within the authority of a power of attorney, a person appointed as a guardian ad litem, or "other person legally authorized to seek the relief." Section 15657.03(a)(2)(B) narrows that last, catch-all category for one specific type of petition: where the petition alleges abuse in the form of isolation, "other person legally authorized to seek the relief" also includes an "interested party" — defined in section 15657.03(b)(3) as an individual with a personal, preexisting relationship with the elder or dependent adult — but only for the purpose of seeking the isolation-specific order described in section 15657.03(b)(5)(E). Separately, section 15657.03(a)(3)(A) allows a petition to be brought on an elder or dependent adult's behalf by a county adult protective services agency, but only where the elder or dependent adult has suffered abuse and has an impaired ability to appreciate and understand the circumstances placing them at risk, or where the elder or dependent adult has given written authorization for the agency to act on their behalf. Two further defined terms from section 15657.03(b) describe the parties once a petition is filed: "Petitioner" means the elder or dependent adult to be protected — not necessarily the person who signed and filed the petition — and, if the petition is granted, the protected person; "Respondent" means the person against whom the protective orders are sought.

expectedJSON.body: Welfare and Institutions Code section 15657.03(b)(5) defines "protective order," for purposes of section 15657.03, to include several categories of restraining order, issuable ex parte, after notice and hearing, or in a judgment. Section 15657.03(b)(5)(A) authorizes a personal-conduct order enjoining a party from abusing, intimidating, molesting, attacking, striking, stalking, threatening, sexually assaulting, battering, harassing, telephoning (including annoying calls under Penal Code section 653m), destroying personal property, contacting (directly or indirectly), or coming within a specified distance of, or disturbing the peace of, the petitioner, and, on a showing of good cause, of other named family or household members or a conservator of the petitioner; the same subparagraph separately authorizes the court, on a showing of good cause, to grant the petitioner exclusive care, possession, or control of an animal, or to order the respondent to stay away from it. Section 15657.03(b)(5)(B) authorizes an order excluding a party from the petitioner's residence or dwelling — but this residence-exclusion order carries an express statutory limit: it may not be issued if legal or equitable title to, or a lease of, the residence is in the sole name of the party to be excluded, or in that party's name together with any other party besides the petitioner. Section 15657.03(b)(5)(C) authorizes an order enjoining other specified behavior the court determines necessary to effectuate either of the first two categories.

expectedJSON.body: Welfare and Institutions Code section 15657.03(c) states the standard for a protective order under this section: with or without notice, an order may issue to restrain any person for the purpose of preventing a recurrence of abuse if a declaration shows, to the satisfaction of the court, reasonable proof of a past act or acts of abuse of the petitioning elder or dependent adult. This standard does not include a separate showing that "great or irreparable harm would result" absent an order — a phrase that appears in California's civil harassment TRO statute, Code of Civil Procedure section 527.6(d), but that is not part of section 15657.03(c)'s text. Once an order issues after notice and a hearing, section 15657.03(i)(1) allows a duration of not more than five years, and allows renewal, on a party's request, for either five additional years or permanently, without a showing of any further abuse since the original order issued; a renewal request may be made at any time within the three months before the order's expiration. Section 15657.03(i)(2) provides that an order silent on its expiration date defaults to a three-year duration from issuance. Separately, section 15657.03(x) states that willful disobedience of a temporary restraining order or restraining order after hearing granted under this section is punishable under Penal Code section 273.6.

expectedJSON.body: Welfare and Institutions Code section 15657.03(y) states that section 15657.03 does not apply to any action or proceeding governed by Chapter 3 (commencing with Section 525) of Title 7 of Part 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure — the chapter that includes California's civil harassment restraining order statute, Code of Civil Procedure section 527.6 — or by Division 10 (commencing with Section 6200) of the Family Code, California's Domestic Violence Prevention Act. Section 15657.03's own eligibility structure, in turn, does not rest on the kind of relationship-based test that governs those two other statutes: it turns instead on whether the person to be protected is an "elder" (65 or older) or a "dependent adult," as defined in sections 15610.27 and 15610.23, and on whether that person has suffered "abuse," as defined in section 15610.07 — with no requirement, as there is for a domestic violence restraining order, that the parties be spouses, cohabitants, dating partners, co-parents, or relatives within a specified degree, and no requirement, as there is for a civil harassment restraining order, that the parties fall outside such a relationship. An elder or dependent adult abused by a spouse, an adult child, a caregiver, or a stranger can each potentially fall within section 15657.03's coverage, provided the abuse and elder/dependent-adult definitions are met; which statute in fact governs a given set of facts depends on the parties' actual relationship and the nature of the alleged conduct.
